setup.text: The imports bring in the tools: text diffing, JSON, the environment, paths, the Bedrock client, and .env loading.
load_dotenv reads the credentials from the .env file next to the script.
IDEAS_PROMPT is the instruction to the model: read the code lines, extract the ideas behind them bottom-up, follow eight rules, and answer as one JSON object.
OLD_RULES adds three rules for a re-run: keep an idea that is still true, drop one that is not, and never reuse an old id for a new idea.

helpers.text: ask sends a prompt to Bedrock and returns the JSON object found in the reply.
write_json writes a list of rows to a file as JSON, one row per line.
load reads one key from a JSON file, or gives None when the file does not exist.
snapshot copies code.json, ideas.json, and diff.json into the next numbered folder under history/.
check verifies the ideas: no duplicate id, no collision with a code id, every source exists and is not the idea itself, and every code line reaches at least one idea.
diff matches old and new code lines by text, then reports the ideas that were added, removed, moved to other sources, or reworded.

main.text: The first stage of main reads the source file and gives each non-blank line an id like C7.
The second stage loads the previous code.json and ideas.json, and builds the extra rules text when old ideas exist.
The third stage writes the numbered lines to code.json.
The fourth stage asks the model for ideas, checks the answer, and on a broken rule sends the answer and the error back for repair, up to three tries.
The fifth stage writes the accepted ideas to ideas.json.
The sixth stage writes diff.json when an old version exists, and deletes a stale diff.json when it does not.
The last stage snapshots the three files into history/ and prints the version.
The guard runs main only when the file runs as a script.
